author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected after booking: the stored date and description are shown for editing, the same validation as booking applies, and a successful correction changes that one visit rather than adding another. Cancelling a visit stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when it is opened for correction, then the same form as booking is shown carrying that visit's stored date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new pair and the owner's record is shown
given a pet holding one visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet still holds exactly one visit
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused and the date is named
given an owner's record, when it is opened, then it offers no way to reach the correction form
a non-goal ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-visit-correction.md records the NG-5 narrowing, which the PRD Non-Goals table and the Visits section already link
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5) and deleting one (NG-4)
a link to the correction form from the owner's record — a follow-up request may add one
recording who corrected a visit or when: the sample carries no visit lifecycle state
notes: ADR obligation: this slice owes a non-goal ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-visit-correction.md, per the convention named in docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md Consequences. It amends that ADR's NG-5 half only; NG-4 is untouched. The PRD already links the path, so a different filename leaves two dangling links. ADRs are system-design-expert territory, so this record carries the obligation rather than the file. Owner-specified constraints recorded at intake, kept out of the PRD as mechanism: the correction form is served at and submitted to the visit's own address under the existing owner and pet path, and it reuses the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template with its visit model attribute. Owner decisions arrived 2026-08-08 and no further product answer is coming; three residual questions were read narrowly and recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions rather than raised as a consultation: whether a past-dated visit can be corrected without moving its date forward (narrow reading: no, booking's date rule is unchanged), whether the owner's record should link to the form (narrow reading: no link now), and whether the correction form lists the pet's other visits (narrow reading: not required).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: A small, local extension of the existing nested owner/pet form-controller pattern inside the `owner` feature package. No new package, type, dependency, template, or persistence path. `docs/system-design.md` § Contracts (Invariants the rows cannot carry) already fixes the write path: `Owner` is the aggregate entry point, a `Visit` persists only through cascade from `Owner`, and no `VisitRepository` exists — so the correction saves through `OwnerRepository.save(owner)` exactly as booking does. The adjustment is confined to `VisitController`: the shared `@ModelAttribute(visit)` loader `loadPetWithVisit` gains an optional `visitId` path variable, and a GET/POST pair is added at /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. Both mechanics have in-repo precedent — `PetController.findPet` already takes an optional `petId` path variable with a null branch, and `PetController` already serves a create/edit pair against one shared template. Basis for the claim: direct reads of `VisitController`, `PetController`, `Owner`, `Pet`, `Visit`, `createOrUpdateVisitForm.html`, and `inputField.html`. The IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so file reads rather than symbol resolution back it — the weaker basis.
integration_points: `loadPetWithVisit` becomes the branch point. It runs before every handler in the controller, so a second `@ModelAttribute(visit)` method is not possible — extension is forced, not chosen. With no `visitId` it keeps returning `new Visit()` plus `pet.addVisit(visit)` (booking, unchanged). With a `visitId` it returns the `Visit` already inside `pet.getVisits()` and calls nothing on the pet.

Form binding mutates the aggregate directly. The loader loads the owner once and puts `owner`, `pet`, and the returned `visit` into the model from that single load, so the bound `visit` IS the instance held in `pet.getVisits()`. Setting date and description onto it is the in-place update; `owners.save(owner)` then cascades a merge that UPDATEs the existing visits row, because the instance carries a non-null id.

No copy step is needed, and this is where the `PetController` precedent misleads. `PetController.updatePetDetails` copies fields onto `owner.getPet(id)` only because `findOwner` and `findPet` each run their own `owners.findById`, yielding two instances from two loads. `VisitController` loads once, so an equivalent `updateVisitDetails` here would copy a value onto itself.

Cascade and collection handling need nothing added. `Pet.visits` is already `cascade = ALL, fetch = EAGER` on a unidirectional `@JoinColumn(pet_id)`, and `@OrderBy(date ASC)` is applied on read — so a corrected date reorders on the next load with no in-memory resorting. There is no `orphanRemoval` and none is wanted; nothing is removed.

The future-date rule currently sits inline in `processNewVisitForm`. Both POST handlers must reject on the identical rule and the identical code `typeMismatch.visitDate`; extract one private helper in a TDD Refactor step so the two cannot drift.
Use `owners.save(owner)`, not `saveAndFlush`. `PetController` flushes to surface the pet-name integrity violation synchronously for its catch block; no constraint on visits needs that.
Success redirects to `redirect:/owners/{ownerId}`; failure returns the view name `pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm`. Both match the booking handler.
`createOrUpdateVisitForm.html` needs no edit — see notes for why, and for the one template line not to touch.
`owners/ownerDetails.html` gains no link. The negative assertion belongs in `OwnerControllerTests`, which is the `@WebMvcTest` that renders that view.

patterns.description: `findPet` — an optional `@PathVariable(name = petId, required = false) Integer petId` on a shared `@ModelAttribute` loader, with a null branch choosing create versus edit. The precedent to copy for `visitId`.
`initUpdateForm` / `processUpdateForm` — the GET/POST edit pair nested under /owners/{ownerId}, sharing one template with the create pair and redirecting to the owner detail page on success.

`getPet(Integer id)` — identity lookup inside the aggregate, returning null when absent. Resolve the visit inside `pet.getVisits()` the same way; a `Pet.getVisit(Integer)` accessor mirroring this is acceptable but not required.

`init` — the fixture shape. Extend it with a persisted `Visit` (id set) added to the pet, and keep a reference: with `OwnerRepository` mocked, the controller mutates the very instance the mock returns, so the in-place update is assertable on real objects without an ArgumentCaptor.

risks.risk: The edit path adds a second visit to the pet. `Pet.visits` is a `LinkedHashSet` and `BaseEntity` declares no `equals`/`hashCode`, so membership is instance identity: a second `Visit` instance carrying the same id becomes a second element, and cascade then writes or duplicates a row.
risks.mitigation: On the edit path never call `pet.addVisit(...)`, never call `owner.addVisit(petId, visit)`, and never construct a `Visit`. Resolve the instance already in `pet.getVisits()` by id. `theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet` catches all three mistakes.

risks.risk: `new Visit()` defaults its date to tomorrow. Constructing one on the edit path silently overwrites the stored date and drops the id.
risks.mitigation: The GET returns the loaded instance unmodified; `theVisitCorrectionFormShouldShowTheStoredDateAndDescription` asserts the stored pair renders.

risks.risk: In-place mutation is inert on a refused submission only because `spring.jpa.open-in-view` is disabled (`docs/system-design.md` § Persistence). The loaded graph is detached, so binding invalid values writes nothing. Enabling open-in-view would flush them and corrupt the stored visit — PRD edge case 4.
risks.mitigation: Treat the disabled open-in-view setting as a guardrail this slice depends on. Assert the refusal with `verify(owners, never()).save(any())`. Note the fixture visit IS mutated in memory by binding, so asserting that its old description survives a refused submission will fail — assert the absent save instead.

risks.risk: An unknown or foreign `visitId`. There is no authentication anywhere (`docs/system-design.md` § Security Context), so resolving the visit within the addressed pet own collection is the only containment against correcting another pet visit through a guessed id.
risks.mitigation: Resolve only inside `pet.getVisits()`; never introduce a global visit lookup. Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when absent, matching the owner-not-found and pet-not-found style already in that method. PRD edge case 3 covers it. This also satisfies `docs/security-principles.md` § Realization, row Trusting cross-request state: every request re-resolves what it acts on.

risks.risk: A success flash message would either hard-code user-facing English — widening the gap the three existing controller flash strings already leave against `REQ-LANG-002` — or add a key that `I18nPropertiesSyncTest` then requires in all eleven bundles.
risks.mitigation: Add no flash message on the correction path. The acceptance criterion asks only that the owner record is shown. A localized confirmation covering all three flows is separate work; if a reviewer wants one, it is a message key in eleven bundles, never a literal.

risks.risk: Mass assignment of the visit id through the form.
risks.mitigation: `setAllowedFields` already disallows `id` and `*.id` for every handler in this controller, and the id arrives only from the path. Leave that binder alone and add no hidden id input to the template.

notes:
Verdict rationale: the accompanying non-goal ADR records a product boundary, not a new architectural pattern, so it does not lift the verdict to `new`. Nothing here is fresh design ground — the aggregate write path, the nested route shape, the shared-template create/edit pair, and the optional-path-variable loader all already exist.

ADR work done in this dispatch: created `docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-visit-correction.md` at the filename the PRD already links from the NG-5 row and the Visits section; amended the NG-5 half of `docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md` additively (status cross-link, one Decision amendment note, one Consequences bullet) leaving NG-4 and the originally recorded text intact; added the index row and the narrowed status to `docs/adr/README.md`.

Template: no edit is needed, and the file stays a read target only. The form carries no `th:action`, so it posts back to the current URL — the edit address — with no change. `th:field` pre-fills date and description from the `visit` model attribute. The heading guard `th:if=${visit[new]}` already drops the New prefix for a persisted visit. One line not to touch: on the Previous Visits row, `th:each` has higher precedence than `th:if` and binds a loop variable also named `visit`, shadowing the model attribute — so that guard filters unsaved visits (it hides the transient one booking adds) rather than switching on form mode. It is not a bug. Consequence: the correction form lists the pet persisted visits including the one being corrected, showing bound values on redisplay. Cosmetic, and `docs/prd.md` Open Questions reads listing other visits as not required.

Guardrails: none needs to change. The ones the slice must respect are the `Owner`-aggregate write path (§ Contracts), the disabled `spring.jpa.open-in-view` (§ Persistence), the unchanged package graph and dependency policy (§ Package Structure, § Dependency Policy), and the `REQ-LANG-002` bundle-parity test. Business rules stay in the controller: `docs/system-design.md` Open Questions item 2 records the no-service-layer gap as undecided, so this slice follows the existing shape and does not repair it.

Deliberately not written now: `docs/system-design.md` § Contracts rows for `Visit`, `OwnerRepository`, and `VisitController` need `REQ-VIS-003` added, and the `VisitController` purpose needs correction alongside booking. That file is a state-only derived brief whose provenance banner says every statement was read off the working tree, so it must not assert code that does not exist yet. This is a doc-sync obligation once the slice lands — recorded here so it is not dropped.

Test placement: `theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoLinkToTheVisitCorrectionForm` belongs in `OwnerControllerTests`, the `@WebMvcTest` that renders `owners/ownerDetails`, not in `VisitControllerTests`. Assert the rendered content carries no visits/.../edit address; do not assert against the template file.

Vocabulary: `docs/ubiquitous-language.md` lists Booking as a term to avoid for a Visit, so use booked only as a participle and never the booking as a noun. No new term is needed for correction, and that file is outside my write scope on a `minor` verdict.

Out of scope and pre-existing: `scripts/doctor.py check` reports project-data spec_version 0.1.0 against manifest 0.2.0 in `scripts/layout.toml`. Not touched.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: findVisit walks pet.getVisits() with a manual for-loop to find a matching id and throw otherwise. The checklist favors stream pipelines over manual loops for this kind of filter-and-find, and the equivalent stream form reads at least as clearly here.
findings.fix: Replace the loop with pet.getVisits().stream().filter(v -> Objects.equals(v.getId(), visitId)).findFirst().orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId() + "."));

findings.description: The explanatory comment above theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoLinkToTheVisitCorrectionForm breaks mid-sentence so that the word "visit's" sits alone on its own line, which reads as a stray line rather than a rewrap. Every other multi-line comment touched in this diff wraps at word boundaries without an orphaned fragment.
findings.fix: Reflow the three-line comment so no line ends on a lone word fragment, e.g. wrap consistently at ~90 columns: "// Correcting a booked visit is reachable only by a reader who already knows the visit's\n// address: REQ-VIS-003 adds no link from the owner's record."

approved_aspects: loadPetWithVisit correctly avoids the copy-then-addVisit pattern: the same aggregate instance loaded once is returned for binding to mutate in place, matching the documented no-second-load design intent
visitId resolution is properly scoped to the addressed pet's own visits (findVisit), so a guessed id cannot reach another pet's visit, and this is exercised by a dedicated test
the future-date rule is correctly factored into one private helper (rejectDateNotInFuture) shared by both POST handlers instead of being duplicated or pushed into a service layer
no template edit, no flash message, and no owner-record link were added, matching the documented deliberate scope boundaries, and the no-link decision is covered by a test
naming follows architecture-principles.md (no prohibited suffixes, no get/set-style verbs on the new private methods), and Javadoc clearly explains the visitId branching semantics
new test names consistently follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD convention from testing-principles.md
./gradlew checkFormat passes with no formatting issues

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Over-binding on the `owner` model attribute. `processVisitCorrectionForm(@ModelAttribute Owner owner, ...)` re-binds the request parameters onto the Owner instance the loader put in the model, and then persists it with `owners.save(owner)`. The `@InitBinder` at :52 disallows only `id`/`*.id`, so every other property of the Owner graph stays bindable, and nothing validates it: `owner` carries no `@Valid`, and the single `BindingResult` belongs to `visit`. Three concrete writes reachable from the new correction POST (all with a well-formed date/description so the handler reaches `save`): (1) `firstName=`, `city=`, `telephone=abc` persist Owner values the owner-edit form refuses, bypassing `@NotBlank`/`@Size(max=30)`/`@Pattern(\d{10})`; (2) `pets[0].name=`/`pets[0].birthDate=...` rewrite a pet outside the addressed visit; (3) `pets[N].name=x` for N beyond the list size auto-grows `Owner.pets` (the getter returns the mutable backing list and `autoGrowNestedPaths` defaults to true), and `@OneToMany(cascade = ALL)` inserts a pet row for that owner. The correction endpoint is therefore a write to the whole Owner aggregate, not to the addressed visit, which also widens the aggregate rule REQ-VIS-003 was designed against (a Visit persisting via cascade from `save(owner)`). The booking handler at :131 is the pre-existing instance of the same class; the fix covers both. Rated `fixable` rather than critical because the application has no authentication and an unauthenticated caller can already reach `/owners/{id}/edit` — the marginal exposure is the validation bypass and the aggregate-wide write, not a new privilege boundary crossing.
findings.fix: Add an attribute-scoped binder alongside the existing one in VisitController: `@InitBinder("owner") void setAllowedOwnerFields(WebDataBinder dataBinder) { dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("*"); }`. Neither visit handler needs any Owner property bound — both use `owner` only as the aggregate root to save (and `owner.addVisit(petId, visit)` in the booking handler) — so blocking every field on that attribute is behavior-preserving for REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-003. Cover it with a test that POSTs the correction with an extra `firstName` (or `pets[1].name`) parameter and asserts the saved owner is unchanged apart from the corrected visit.

approved_aspects: Containment holds for the ownerId/petId/visitId triple: the loader resolves the owner by id, the pet through `owner.getPet(petId)`, and the visit through the private `findVisit(Pet, Integer)` scan of that pet's own collection. There is no global visit lookup and no VisitRepository, so a guessed visitId cannot reach another pet's or another owner's visit on either the GET or the POST — both share the one `@ModelAttribute` loader, so neither path can be addressed without passing all three checks.

Mass assignment on the form-bound `visit` is contained despite the deliberate absence of a copy step: `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` keeps the identifier unbindable, so a submitted `id=<other pet's visit>` cannot redirect the cascaded merge at another visit row (the one bypass that would have defeated findVisit). Visit's only other bindable properties are `date` and `description`, exactly the pair REQ-VIS-003 replaces, and both stay under `@Valid`/`@NotBlank` plus the shared future-date rule.

A refused correction persists nothing: `processVisitCorrectionForm` returns the form view before reaching `owners.save(owner)`, and with `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` the loaded aggregate is detached, so the in-place mutation binding performed is never flushed. The refusal tests assert the absent save, which is the property that actually holds.

The new `IllegalArgumentException` message interpolates only the `Integer` visitId and the pet id — no user-controlled string reaches it, so the recorded error-page detail defect cannot be turned into reflected XSS through this path. The leak is limited to confirming which visit ids belong to a pet, which the address itself already reveals.

`@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false)` reads only URI template variables, so a `?visitId=` query parameter cannot populate it and the unchanged `/visits/new` booking flow still takes the null branch. The optional-path-variable shape matches the existing precedent in OwnerController.findOwner and PetController.
The correction writes through `owners.save(owner)` only, honoring the aggregate rule that a Visit persists via cascade from the owner root; no VisitRepository or direct visit write was introduced.

`createOrUpdateVisitForm.html` renders every value through `th:text` (no `th:utext`, no inline JavaScript), so the corrected description round-trips escaped; the form posts to the current URL, so the correction POST cannot be retargeted at the booking route.

Supply chain surface unchanged: the change set touches no build file, dependency declaration, or lockfile (docs, one controller, two test classes), so there is no new third-party code to verify against the NVD for this pass.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 4 has two clauses: 'a refused correction leaves the stored visit as it was, AND redisplays the submitted values for another attempt.' Both refusal tests pin the first clause correctly with verify(owners, never()).save(any()) — deliberately, per the design triage, since binding has already mutated the detached in-memory visit by the time the handler refuses, so asserting the visit's former field values would not hold. But neither test asserts the second clause: that the submitted values are shown back on redisplay. Since the bound visit IS the model attribute, asserting e.g. model().attribute("visit", hasProperty("date", is(<submitted future date>))) in the blank-description test, and model().attribute("visit", hasProperty("description", is(<submitted description>))) in the date-refusal test, would pin the redisplay half at no extra setup cost. As written, a regression that redisplayed stale or blanked-out values instead of the reader's own submission would pass both tests.
findings.fix: Add a model attribute assertion in each refusal test confirming the submitted value for the field that did NOT fail validation is redisplayed unchanged (e.g. the valid future date in the blank-description test; the valid description in the date-refusal test).

findings.description: Four-phase structure (testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure) asks for blank lines separating Act from Assert. Both tests run the mockMvc.perform(...).andExpect(...) chain (Act+first Assert) directly followed by a further assertThat(...) line with no blank line before it, unlike the sibling tests in the same file (e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheStoredVisitInPlace, the two refusal tests) which do separate the trailing verify/assertThat with a blank line.
findings.fix: Insert a blank line before the trailing assertThat(...) statement in both tests, matching the spacing already used in the other new tests in this file.

findings.description: Three-Tier Data Naming (testing-principles.md): the literal "Vaccination and dental check" (an irrelevant/Tier-2 description — its content never drives an assertion, only its non-blankness matters) and LocalDate.now().plusDays(9) (an irrelevant future date) are each repeated verbatim as bare literals across four tests instead of being named once. theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheStoredVisitInPlace already names its own local copies (correctedDate, correctedDescription); the other three tests inline the same values unnamed, so the vocabulary is inconsistent within one file the diff just touched.
findings.fix: Extract a class-level constant or small factory (e.g. SOME_FUTURE_VISIT_DATE, SOME_VISIT_DESCRIPTION, or a correctedVisitDate()/correctedVisitDescription() helper) and reuse it across the four tests instead of repeating the raw literals.

approved_aspects: The verify(owners, never()).save(any()) refusal assertion correctly pins PRD edge case 4's 'stored visit untouched' clause given the recorded detached-entity mechanism (open-in-view disabled) — asserting the visit's former field values would not have held, as the triage noted.

theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet genuinely catches the LinkedHashSet + missing equals/hashCode trap: containsExactly(bookedVisit) fails on size alone if a second Visit instance carrying the same id were added via addVisit.

The pre-existing booking tests (initNewVisitForm, processNewVisitFormSuccess, processNewVisitFormHasErrors, processNewVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture) still pass unmodified after loadPetWithVisit gained the optional visitId path variable; the null-visitId branch is unchanged and verified by the full test run.

theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotThePets correctly exercises PRD edge case 3 (a not-found visit id, whether foreign or nonexistent, is refused rather than recording a new visit) and asserts both the thrown IllegalArgumentException and the absent save.

theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoLinkToTheVisitCorrectionForm correctly lands in OwnerControllerTests (the @WebMvcTest rendering ownerDetails) rather than VisitControllerTests, matching the design triage's placement note.
VisitController.java line coverage is 92% (13/167 lines uncovered) per jacocoTestReport, comfortably above the brief's 80% target.

author: feature-implementer
notes: Round-1 review findings applied; all seven accepted, none rejected. security-reviewer (over-binding on the owner model attribute): added @InitBinder("owner") setting setDisallowedFields("*") in VisitController, and scoped the pre-existing binder to @InitBinder("visit"). Deviation from the literal fix, which said 'alongside the existing one': WebDataBinder.setDisallowedFields REPLACES rather than accumulates, and Spring invokes @InitBinder methods in reflection-discovery order, so an unscoped binder that also applies to owner could overwrite ("*") with ("id","*.id") depending on method ordering. Attribute-scoping both binders makes the outcome order-independent and matches PetController's existing @InitBinder("owner")/@InitBinder("pet") pair (basis: grep over src/main/java for @InitBinder; no IDE oracle connected this run, so the weaker basis). Behavior-preserving: visit and owner are the only bound model attributes in this controller, and disallowedFields is inert for the @PathVariable simple-type binders. New test theVisitCorrectionShouldIgnoreOwnerParametersOnTheForm posts firstName=, telephone=abc, pets[0].name= and pets[1].name=x alongside a valid correction and asserts the owner's firstName, telephone, pet count and pet name are unchanged while the visit description is corrected; verified red by renaming the binder's attribute (test FAILED), then green after restoring it. All four pre-existing booking tests still pass, so owner.addVisit(petId, visit) is unaffected. test-reviewer: both refusal tests now assert the PRD edge-case-4 redisplay clause (submitted date redisplayed in the blank-description test, submitted description in the date-refusal test); blank line inserted before the trailing assertThat in theVisitCorrectionFormShouldShowTheStoredDateAndDescription and theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet; the repeated literals are now SOME_CORRECTED_VISIT_DATE and SOME_CORRECTED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION (SOME_ prefix per the Tier-2 irrelevant-data convention) reused across all five correction tests. code-quality-reviewer: findVisit is now a stream filter/findFirst/orElseThrow with the same IllegalArgumentException message; the orphaned comment fragment above theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoLinkToTheVisitCorrectionForm is reflowed. IDE static-analysis pre-check: not run (IDE not consulted). Out of scope as instructed: docs/ untouched, scripts/doctor.py spec_version failure not addressed.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Round-1 over-binding finding (VisitController owner model attribute) is closed. Verified on the code, not the claim: the two @ModelAttribute-bound attributes in this controller are exactly `visit` (the @ModelAttribute("visit") method plus the `@Valid Visit visit` handler param, whose derived attribute name is `visit`) and `owner` (`@ModelAttribute Owner owner`, derived name `owner`). Both named binders match. Nothing else in the controller is request-bound: `pet` and `minVisitDate` are model-only (no handler param binds them), and `ownerId`/`petId`/`visitId` are simple-type @PathVariable binders where disallowedFields is inert (that binder is used for conversion, not field binding). So scoping the formerly global binder to `visit` leaves no bound attribute that lost its `id`/`*.id` protection - no `id` can now be bound where it previously could not.

setDisallowedFields("*") does block the nested paths, not just top-level Owner properties. DataBinder.checkAllowedFields runs first in doBind and drops every PropertyValue whose canonical name matches a disallowed pattern; PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch treats the single-character pattern `*` as matching any name, so `pets[0].name`, `pets[1].name`, and `pets[0].visits[0].*` are all filtered. Because the filtering happens before applyPropertyValues, the BeanWrapper never touches `pets[1]` and the auto-grow that would produce a cascade insert never occurs. WebDataBinder's field markers are no bypass either: `_pets` and `!firstName` are rewritten into plain `pets`/`firstName` PropertyValues in WebDataBinder.doBind and then filtered by the same `*` check in super.doBind. All three writes described in round 1 - bypassing Owner bean validation, rewriting a pet outside the addressed visit, and auto-growing Owner.pets into a cascade insert - are unreachable from both the correction POST and the booking POST, since @InitBinder applies per attribute name across the whole controller.

The implementer's deviation (scoping the pre-existing binder to `visit` instead of leaving it unscoped) is the right call and its reasoning holds. setDisallowedFields assigns rather than accumulates, and @InitBinder discovery order is unspecified, so an unscoped binder matching `owner` could have overwritten ("*") with ("id","*.id") depending on reflection order - a silent reopening. No @ControllerAdvice or other global @InitBinder exists in src/main (grep for InitBinder/ControllerAdvice: only OwnerController, PetController, VisitController), so no external binder can overwrite either. PetController's @InitBinder("owner")/@InitBinder("pet") pair is a genuine precedent for the shape.

theVisitCorrectionShouldIgnoreOwnerParametersOnTheForm proves what it claims and is a real regression detector, not a tautology. Each parameter it sends would produce an observable write without the binder: `firstName=""` would bind the empty string over "George" (no StringTrimmerEditor with emptyAsNull is registered), `telephone` would take an unvalidated value past the @Pattern the owner form enforces, `pets[0].name=""` would blank the addressed pet, and `pets[1].name` would auto-grow pets to size 2. The four assertions pin exactly those, and the fixture now seeds real values (OWNER_FIRST_NAME, OWNER_TELEPHONE, PET_NAME) so the assertions can fail. The trailing assertion that the description was still corrected keeps the test from passing for the wrong reason (a wholesale rejected POST). Confirmed green: ./gradlew test --tests '*VisitControllerTests*' passes.

findVisit's rewrite to stream filter/findFirst/orElseThrow preserves the containment exactly: the search domain is still pet.getVisits() for the addressed pet only, so a guessed or attacker-supplied visitId belonging to another pet or another owner still cannot resolve, and the IllegalArgumentException message is byte-identical. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotThePets still pins that path.

No supply-chain surface in this delta: build.gradle and the dependency set are untouched (delta is VisitController.java plus VisitControllerTests.java), so the round-1 dependency verification still stands. No secrets, no new logging of PII, no string-concatenated queries, and no user-derived content newly rendered - the redisplayed form values go through Thymeleaf's escaping as before.
